雅思早间任务 · 第 6 周第 1 天（11 月 25 日 周三）

今天的主题：压力、心理健康和工作生活平衡。这是雅思 G 类的超高频话题：大作文常考「现代人为什么压力越来越大，怎么解决」「公司该不该限制加班」；听力 Section 4 和阅读里的心理学研究也常出现 chronic、anxiety、cope、conduct research 这类词；口语 Part 1 会直接问 Do you often feel stressed? How do you relax?。今天是第 6 周第一天，强化期继续，每个词后面 ≈ 是同义替换，背的时候连同义词一起记。

例句

  • Many office workers suffer from chronic stress because of their heavy workload.（很多上班族因为工作量太大而长期承受压力。）
  • Students often find it hard to cope with exam pressure.（学生常常觉得很难应对考试压力。）
  • Regular exercise is one of the best ways to combat anxiety.（规律运动是对抗焦虑最好的办法之一。）
  • The study was conducted by a team of psychologists.（这项研究是由一组心理学家进行的。）
  • There is no single approach that works for everyone.（没有一种方法适合所有人。）

同义替换小抄（听力最常见的考法）：

题目写 deal with / handle → 录音可能说 cope with　|　题目写 long-term → 录音说 chronic　|　题目写 carry out a study → 录音说 conduct research　|　题目写 fight / tackle → 录音说 combat　|　题目写 worry → 录音说 anxiety / nerves　|　题目写 relaxing → 录音说 restful　|　题目写 suggest → 录音说 recommend

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，并能说出至少 15 个词的一个同义替换。再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 pressure、cope、workload、reduce 写一句「现代人工作压力大，公司应该怎么做」，大作文能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Why are we all so stressed?（我们为什么都压力这么大？），4 月 23 日这一期。Neil 和 Becca 聊现代人的压力：什么是 overwhelm（不堪重负），长期压力怎样导致 burnout（精力耗尽），考试紧张为什么反而能帮你发挥，以及心理学家 Claudia Hammond 的减压建议。这集 6 分钟左右，Claudia Hammond 的三段采访最难。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。节目后面照样有一组我按雅思格式出的题（选择 Q1–3 + 笔记填空 Q4–9）。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，像考试一样做下面的 Q1–9，只听一遍，听完点「对答案」。选择题注意：两个人各说一种情况时，要分清题目问的是谁；小测验要听到最后公布的答案，不是主持人猜的那个。
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Claudia Hammond 讲 overwhelm 那段语速快、有重复和口头语（kind of、you know），先读懂中文再听。
  4. 第三遍挑 Becca 解释 chronic 和 burnout 那段（"Feeling overwhelmed and unable to cope with life..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：overwhelm（不堪重负）、chronic（长期的）、burnout（精力耗尽）、nerves（紧张）、one-size-fits-all（一刀切的）、to-do list（待办清单）。

Questions 1–9（按雅思格式自编）

Questions 1–3　Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

1 What makes Becca feel most stressed?
A not having enough time to finish something　B trying something new that she is not good at　C worrying about the news

2 How does Neil deal with stressful situations?
A He tells himself to practise more.　B He slows down and takes a breath.　C He goes for a walk in nature.

3 According to Claudia Hammond's research, the most restful activity is
A reading for pleasure.　B walking in nature.　C listening to music.

Questions 4–9　Complete the notes below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.

Stress and how to manage it

• Many young people describe their feelings with the word 4

• In this state, people feel overloaded and feel they cannot 5

• If the stress becomes long-term, it may finally lead to 6

• During an exam, nerves can 7 your thinking

• It is OK to be 'good enough' instead of always aiming for 8

• A to-do list that never ends is simply a sign of a 9 life

答案：1 B　2 B　3 A　4 overwhelm　5 cope　6 burnout　7 sharpen　8 perfection　9 busy。同义替换提示：题目 deal with = 录音 cope with；题目 long-term = 录音 chronic / in the longer term；题目 finally = 录音 in the end；题目 aiming for = 录音 trying for；题目 is simply a sign of = 录音 is just signs of。第 1 题 A 是 Neil 的答案，是干扰项；第 2 题 A 是 Becca 的做法；第 3 题 B 是 Neil 猜的，最后公布的答案是 A。

点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Neil：Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.

Neil：大家好，这里是 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是尼尔。

Becca：And I'm Becca. Worrying about work or exams, war and climate change in the news. It's no wonder难怪 that modern life is stressful. What makes you stress, Neil?

Becca：我是贝卡。担心工作或考试，新闻里又是战争又是气候变化，难怪现代生活让人压力这么大。尼尔，什么事会让你有压力？

Neil：Oh, good question. I think not having enough time to do something, that really makes me stressed out压力很大的. How about you?

Neil：好问题。我觉得是没有足够的时间做完一件事，这真的会让我压力山大。你呢？

Becca：Um. When I'm trying to do something that I've never tried before and I'm not very good at it, that makes me feel really stressed.

Becca：嗯，当我在做一件以前从没试过、而且不太擅长的事情时，我会觉得压力特别大。

Neil：I find that stressful, too.

Neil：我也觉得那样很有压力。

Becca：And how do you cope应对，应付 with stressful situations, Neil?

Becca：那你是怎么应对有压力的情况的，尼尔？

Neil：Well, I try to slow down, uh, pause, take a breath深呼吸 and think, 'at some point在某个时候, probably later today, everything will be okay again.' How about you?

Neil：我会试着放慢节奏，停一下，深呼吸，然后想：「过一会儿，可能今天晚些时候，一切又都会好起来的。」你呢？

Becca：Yeah, same. But in my mind, I'm telling myself that, 'I will be better at what I'm doing. I just need to practise more.'

Becca：嗯，我也一样。不过我心里会对自己说：「我会越做越好的，只是需要多练习。」

Neil：Hmm. Many young people who feel stressed about the modern world use the word overwhelm不堪重负（的感觉） to describe their feelings. And overwhelm不堪重负（的感觉） was also the topic of a recent BBC World Service programme, What in the World. Here's Iqra Farooq and Claudia Hammond.

Neil：嗯。很多对现代社会感到有压力的年轻人会用 overwhelm（不堪重负）这个词来形容自己的感受。overwhelm 也是 BBC 国际台最近一期节目《What in the World》的主题。下面来听伊克拉·法鲁克和克劳迪娅·哈蒙德的对话。

Claudia Hammond：So, overwhelm不堪重负（的感觉） is an emotional情绪的 state where you are struggling挣扎，吃力 with your current situation. So, you might feel overloaded（使）负担过重, you might feel you can't cope应对，应付, and that might be a temporary暂时的 thing, hopefully. But if it's not in the longer term, if that becomes more of a kind of chronic长期的，慢性的 kind of stress, then that might lead to burnout精力耗尽，过劳倦怠 in the end最终.

Claudia Hammond：所谓 overwhelm，是一种情绪状态：你在当前的处境里苦苦挣扎。你可能觉得负担过重，觉得自己应付不过来。希望这只是暂时的。但如果不是暂时的，如果它变成一种长期的、慢性的压力，最终可能会导致精力耗尽（burnout）。

Becca：Feeling overwhelmed不堪重负（的感觉） and unable to cope应对，应付 with life can become chronic长期的，慢性的, meaning that it lasts for a long time. Overwhelm不堪重负（的感觉） can lead to burnout精力耗尽，过劳倦怠, mental or physical exhaustion筋疲力尽 caused by working too hard.

Becca：感到不堪重负、应付不了生活，这种状态可能会变成 chronic，意思是持续很长时间。overwhelm 可能导致 burnout，也就是因为工作过度而造成的精神或身体上的极度疲惫。

Neil：So, how can we manage the stress in our lives and feel happier and healthier? That's what we'll be discussing in this episode, along with some useful new words and phrases. You'll find all the vocabulary from this episode on our website bbclearningenglish.com.

Neil：那么，我们怎样才能管理好生活中的压力，让自己更快乐、更健康呢？这就是我们这一期要讨论的内容，同时还会学一些有用的新单词和短语。本期所有词汇都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

Becca：But before we start, I have a question for you, Neil. One simple way of combating对抗，减少 stress is taking time to rest. So, according to research conducted进行（研究） by BBC presenter and psychologist心理学家 Claudia Hammond, which activity is thought to be the most restful让人放松的? Is it:
a) reading for pleasure为了消遣,
b) walking in nature, or
c) listening to music?

Becca：不过开始之前，我有个问题要问你，尼尔。对抗压力的一个简单办法就是花时间休息。根据 BBC 主持人、心理学家克劳迪娅·哈蒙德做的研究，哪种活动被认为最能让人放松？是 a) 为消遣而阅读，b) 在大自然里散步，还是 c) 听音乐？

Neil：Well, I think they're all quite relaxing, but I'm gonna guess
b) walking in nature.

Neil：嗯，我觉得都挺放松的，不过我猜 b) 在大自然里散步。

Becca：I'm surprised, Neil! I know you love music. And we'll find out the answer later. One of the most stressful things facing many young people is exams. Here, Claudia Hammond offers some advice for managing exam stress to BBC World Service's What in the World:

Becca：真意外，尼尔！我知道你很爱音乐。答案我们稍后揭晓。很多年轻人面临的最有压力的事情之一就是考试。下面克劳迪娅·哈蒙德在 BBC 国际台的《What in the World》节目里给出了一些应对考试压力的建议：

Claudia Hammond：…particularly in the exam itself, if you feel stressed, then just knowing that you may well很可能 perform表现，发挥 better while you're stressed, that this… it concentrates the mind使头脑集中、清醒, it sharpens使敏锐，使清晰 and you know nervesnerves：紧张，焦虑（非正式） sharpen使敏锐，使清晰 your thinking and allow you to really do your best.

Claudia Hammond：……尤其是在考场上，如果你感到紧张，只要知道人在有压力的时候反而很可能发挥得更好就行了。压力会让你集中精神，让头脑更敏锐。紧张感会让你的思维更清晰，让你真正发挥出最好的水平。

Neil：It's normal to feel nervesnerves：紧张，焦虑（非正式） before an exam. Nervesnerves：紧张，焦虑（非正式） is an informal非正式的 word for worry or anxiety焦虑, but according to Claudia, nervesnerves：紧张，焦虑（非正式） aren't necessarily bad.

Neil：考试前紧张很正常。nerves 是表示担心或焦虑的非正式说法。不过照克劳迪娅的说法，紧张不一定是坏事。

Becca：Yes, nervesnerves：紧张，焦虑（非正式） can help concentrate the mind使头脑集中、清醒. The phrase concentrate or sharpen使敏锐，使清晰 the mind means to think more clearly about something like an actor or an athlete feeling nervesnerves：紧张，焦虑（非正式） before a big performance can help them do their best.

Becca：对，紧张能帮人集中精神。concentrate the mind 或 sharpen the mind 这个说法的意思是让人把某件事想得更清楚。比如演员或运动员在大型演出或比赛前感到紧张，反而能帮他们发挥出最好水平。

Neil：Claudia recommends other ways to reduce stress as well. These include slowing down and accepting that it's ok to be 'good enough' rather than always trying for perfection完美. Here, she shares more top tips最实用的建议 with Iqra Farooq for BBC World Service's What in the World:

Neil：克劳迪娅还推荐了其他减压方法，包括放慢节奏，以及接受「够好就行」，而不是总追求完美。下面她在 BBC 国际台《What in the World》节目里和伊克拉·法鲁克分享了更多实用建议：

Iqra Farooq：I guess it's - there's no one-size-fits-all一刀切的，适合所有人的 as well, when it comes to说到，谈到 this. So, if someone's listening and thinking, 'I want some top tips最实用的建议 on just feeling overwhelmed不堪重负（的感觉） generally in my life,' what would you say to them?

Iqra Farooq：我觉得说到这件事，也没有一种适合所有人的办法。那么，如果有人在听节目时想：「我总体上觉得生活让我不堪重负，想要几条最实用的建议」，你会对他们说什么？

Claudia Hammond：So, first I would say accept that your to-do list待办清单 is never going to end, it's always going to be there. So, even I know that might sound defeatist消极认输的, but even if you get to the end of it today, tomorrow there will be something else on it. And that's just life, and that is just signs of a busy life.

Claudia Hammond：首先我会说：接受你的待办清单永远不会做完，它会一直在那儿。我知道这听起来可能有点消极认输，但就算你今天把清单上的事都做完了，明天上面还会有新的事情。这就是生活，这只是生活忙碌的表现。

Becca：There are many ways to combat对抗，减少 stress, not a one-size-fits-all一刀切的，适合所有人的 solution. The phrase, one-size-fits-all一刀切的，适合所有人的, describes trying to apply the same solution to many different problems.

Becca：对抗压力的方法有很多，并没有一种一刀切的解决办法。one-size-fits-all 这个说法，指的是试图用同一个办法去解决很多不同的问题。

Neil：Claudia's final piece of advice is don't worry too much about your to-do-list, the list of all the items you have to do. Why? Because it never ends. Every day there will be something new to add to the list. So, why stress?

Neil：克劳迪娅最后一条建议是：别太担心你的待办清单，也就是列着你所有要做的事情的清单。为什么？因为它永远做不完，每天都会有新的事要加进去。那又何必为此焦虑呢？

Becca：Some good advice there, Neil. I think I'll try these techniques技巧，方法 next time I feel stressed. And, speaking of说到 ways to de-stress减压 reminds me of my question I asked you earlier. According to research conducted进行（研究） by BBC presenter and psychologist心理学家 Claudia Hammond, which activity is thought of to be the most restful让人放松的? And you answered
b) walking in nature. Unfortunately, Neil, the answer is
a) reading.

Becca：这些建议都不错，尼尔。我想下次感到有压力时，我会试试这些方法。说到减压的办法，我想起了之前问你的问题：根据 BBC 主持人、心理学家克劳迪娅·哈蒙德做的研究，哪种活动被认为最能让人放松？你选的是 b) 在大自然里散步。很遗憾，尼尔，答案是 a) 阅读。

Neil：Ah well, reading is really relaxing as well.

Neil：啊，好吧，阅读确实也很放松。

Becca：OK, let's recap回顾，概括 the vocabulary from this episode, beginning with the adjective chronic长期的，慢性的, which means continuing for a long time.

Becca：好，我们来回顾一下本期的词汇。先是形容词 chronic，意思是持续很长时间的。

Neil：Burnout精力耗尽，过劳倦怠 is a feeling of physical or mental exhaustion筋疲力尽 caused by working too hard.

Neil：burnout 是因为工作过度而产生的身体或精神上的极度疲惫感。

Becca：If you say that a difficult situation sharpens使敏锐，使清晰 or concentrates someone's mind, you mean that it makes them think clearly.

Becca：如果你说某个困难的处境 sharpens 或 concentrates someone's mind，意思是它让人头脑更清醒、想得更清楚。

Neil：Nervesnerves：紧张，焦虑（非正式） are an informal非正式的 word for worry or anxiety焦虑.

Neil：nerves 是表示担心或焦虑的非正式说法。

Becca：A one-size-fits-all一刀切的，适合所有人的 approach方法 tries to apply the same solution to all problems, rather than solving them individually单独地，逐个地.

Becca：one-size-fits-all（一刀切）的方法，是用同一个办法去解决所有问题，而不是一个个分别解决。

See you again next time, but for now it's goodbye!

过关标准：Q1–9 答对 7 题以上；不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（overwhelm 和 burnout 是什么、考试紧张为什么不一定是坏事、Claudia 给了哪些减压建议）；Becca 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. She suffers from ______ back pain that has lasted for years.（长期的）
  2. After working 70 hours a week, he was close to ______.（精力耗尽）
  3. It's hard to ______ with a new job and a new baby at the same time.（应对）
  4. The government has introduced new measures to ______ air pollution.（对抗，治理）
  5. The survey was ______ among 2,000 university students.（进行）
  6. Many people feel ______ by the amount of information online.（不堪重负的）
点开看答案

开头那题选 a，阅读（reading for pleasure），Neil 猜的 b 散步不对。填空：1. chronic 2. burnout 3. cope 4. combat 5. conducted 6. overwhelmed

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 1 / Part 3 做准备）：What do you usually do when you feel stressed? 用英语说两三句：When I feel stressed, I usually ... because ... / It helps me ...。Part 3 再想一层：Why do you think people today feel more stressed than in the past?（可以用 workload、pressure、technology、never-ending to-do list）
